note.question: Can an online mediator obtain truthful bargaining ranges and recommend a mutually acceptable, efficient compromise without knowing parties' cardinal utilities or beliefs?
note.overview: Two privately informed negotiators report bargaining ranges to an automated mediator and can veto its proposed bundle. The paper characterizes mechanisms for which truth telling is a dominant strategy and acceptance is individually rational, with ex post efficiency.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

models.name: Strategy-Proof Multi-Issue Mediation model
models.summary: Two privately informed negotiators report bargaining ranges to an automated mediator and can veto its proposed bundle. The paper characterizes mechanisms for which truth telling is a dominant strategy and acceptance is individually rational, with ex post efficiency.
objects: Negotiator 1 with a private bargaining range and preferences
Negotiator 2 with a private bargaining range and opposing issue rankings
inputs: Each negotiator privately knows own type and utility ordering over acceptable bundles
The mediator solicits bargaining ranges, not cardinal utilities or priors
Finite alternative sets and opposed rankings within each issue are public
The outside option separates negotiable alternatives from private deal breakers
Admissible utility profiles satisfy the maintained monotonicity and, for positive existence, quid-pro-quo restriction
decisions: Each negotiator reports a bargaining-range type
The mediator maps reports to a logrolling bundle or impasse
Each negotiator accepts or vetoes the recommendation

assumptions: There are exactly two negotiators and two finite ordered issues, one main and one supplementary
Preferences over each individual issue are diametrically opposed after efficiency reduction

models.method: Inspired by the structured mediation programs that are offered by the ODR systems, we follow a mechanism design approach to develop a tractable framework in search of efficient, incentive-compatible, and impartial mediation mechanisms.

sources.section: 4. Special Members of the Logrolling Family
sources.quote: Within the family of logrolling mechanisms, this is achieved simply by assigning the highest precedence to a median logroll­ ing bundle, the next precedence to those bundles that are closest to the chosen median, and so on, and the lowest precedence to the extremal logrolling bundles.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Each negotiator privately learns a type identified by the least acceptable main-issue alternative. In the announcement stage, both report types to the mediator. The mechanism proposes a two-issue bundle or the outside option. In the ratification stage, both parties simultaneously accept or veto; agreement occurs only with unanimous acceptance, otherwise both receive the outside option.

components.label: Dominant-strategy truthful-reporting equilibrium with unanimous acceptance
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Dominant-strategy truthful-reporting equilibrium with unanimous acceptance. The revelation argument reduces voluntary mediation to a two-stage direct mechanism with veto rights. Truthful reporting is a dominant-strategy equilibrium and proposals are never vetoed exactly when f is strategy-proof and individually rational. Theorems 1-2 characterize all such efficient mechanisms as quid-pro-quo logrolling mechanisms.
